findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process … executed with Tool-level rigor” names rubric patterns the agent does not need to run the wizard.
findings.fix: Keep the factory-subcommand rule and its explanation of failures at dispatch. Remove only the pattern labels and record that removal.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” does not name stale-provider diagnosis as an entry point or distinguish setup from running an already configured review or execution.
findings.fix: Use this skill to set up or refresh ai-kit’s cross-AI review and execute lanes: choose which installed CLIs and models should review or code, order each role’s fallbacks, and confirm effort and opt-ins before writing the [lanes] roster in config.toml. Use it when a review or execute run offers setup because no lanes exist, when the user asks which reviewers are available or which configured OpenCode providers are stale, or when they ask about migrating review-spec.toml. Use --check-only to report availability without changing ai-kit configuration, persistent caches, or trust. Default to ./.aikit/config.toml; --local or --global selects the layer, not permission to replace its roster. Announce the exact path and ask before replacing an existing roster. Not for running a configured review or execution, editing unrelated TOML tables, or changing provider credentials.

findings.evidence: “When the write target was local … check whether it holds a command-bearing entry” begins a 30-line trust procedure loaded even for global, headless, and check-only runs. The main file is 494 lines and 7,183 words despite already having a trust reference.
findings.fix: Keep the fail-closed rule and the exact trigger in Step 4. Move the full preview, per-role reconciliation, migration, consent, and revoke procedure into references/config-file.md under Trust; direct Step 4 to read it only after a confirmed command-bearing local write or when recovering from an untrusted-roster warning outside --check-only.

findings.evidence: “--global forces <user config> directly” and “--local also forces local directly” each skip the target question, but no rule handles both flags together.
findings.fix: Declare --local and --global mutually exclusive. If both are supplied, stop before saving caches or selecting a target and ask the owner to rerun with exactly one.

findings.evidence: “If the proposal shows an alias group” can pass when the group is omitted entirely. The linked lanes.md is a prose excerpt and does not seed the catalog row the proposal actually consumes.
findings.fix: Supply a deterministic alias catalog and runtime snapshot, then assert that the matching alias row is present under the printed assumed label with no rank or score. Keep the assertion that no heuristic question is asked.

findings.evidence: The set is balanced 10/10, but negatives such as “Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill” are easy rejections, and the only execute-setup positive also asks for review setup.
findings.fix: Keep the 10/10 split. Replace unrelated negatives with near-misses such as checking OpenCode providers without touching ai-kit or running an existing execute lane, and add an execute-only positive phrased as choosing a coding model and fallbacks before starting work.

findings.evidence: “fetch-model-catalog … --if-stale --jev” omits --cwd. When detection finds an installed runtime with no models list, the helper resolves and may migrate the roster at its process cwd, even though Step 1.5 evaluated consent against the separately resolved project root. The later refresh supplies --cwd but does not carry forward the keep-backup environment.
findings.fix: Pass --cwd "<project root>" on every catalog fetch. Make Step 1.5’s fetch authorization and backup choice apply to all fetch forms and retries, including unmatched-candidate refresh and forced refresh. Do not allow those paths to bypass a blocked migration.

findings.evidence: “Each object in lanes carries: key; runtime and model …” omits vendor after Step 2.3 explicitly resolves it or asks the owner for it. The selector in quota.py reads the stored vendor; without it, the confirmation is lost and the cross-vendor filter cannot distinguish the lane correctly.
findings.fix: Carry the resolved or owner-confirmed vendor into every modeled lane object, including custom modeled lanes, and add it to the config-file.md example. Leave vendor unset for an unpinned session default rather than guessing.

findings.evidence: “single seats the first available lane of the review order; double also seats an independent secondary” does not match resolve_reviewers. With an available same-vendor lane first and an available different-vendor lane second, single selects the second lane. Double can return only one reviewer.
findings.fix: Explain that single takes the first available different-vendor lane in ladder order, falling back to the first available same-vendor lane. Double takes the first available primary in ladder order and adds a different-vendor secondary only if one is available.

findings.evidence: “For every saved lane … Step 4 shows the … lines config-status prints” conflates the saved file with the effective project roster. config-status can omit newly written global lanes under local-only, include inherited lanes after a local write, or emit no capability rows before local trust.
findings.fix: Label config-status output as the effective roster for the resolved project, not as a preview of every saved lane. Keep the saved orders read from rendered.toml separate, explain when the selected layer is shadowed or pending, and rerun config-status after the owner explicitly grants trust.

findings.evidence: “config = cfg_resolve('<project root>', …)” puts an absolute path into Python source as a quoted literal. A valid directory such as an owner’s checkout with an apostrophe in its name breaks the probe planning snippet before the write-risk review.
findings.fix: Pass the project root and helper directory as separate quoted argv values and read them from sys.argv. If the preflight fails or emits invalid JSON, run no live probe, report availability as unknown, and continue to the stale-provider report.
